descriptionChirho: Spatial preposition/adverb indicating a position directly across from or facing something. Greek κατέναντι used for physical spatial orientation. Spanish 'frente a, enfrente' (facing, opposite); Hindi सामने (in front of, facing); Arabic مُقَابِلَ (opposite, facing); Korean 맞은편에 (on the opposite side); Swahili mkabala na (opposite to). This sense emphasizes the spatial relationship of two entities facing each other across a space, as in Mark 11:2 'the village opposite you' and Mark 13:3 'opposite the temple'.

Preposition indicating being in the sight of or in the presence of a person, often with a sense of accountability or witness. Greek κατέναντι used for relational 'before' rather than purely spatial opposition. Spanish 'delante de' (in front of, before); Hindi सामने (before, in the presence of); Arabic أَمامَ (before, in front of); Korean 앞에서 (in front of, before); Swahili mbele ya (before, in front of). Used in contexts like Romans 4:17 'before God' and 2 Corinthians 2:17 'in the sight of God', where the emphasis is on being under observation or in relational proximity rather than physical opposition.
